description: A qualitative analysis application you use in conversation with Claude, compatible with QualCoder: create projects, read, search and code your qualitative data, edit the codebook, write memos and export, in project files on this computer.
long_description:
Exegete (formerly qualcoder-mcp) is a qualitative analysis application you use in conversation with Claude, compatible with QualCoder. With Claude, you start projects, bring in documents and transcripts, read them with their codings, search, code them with suggestions you approve, edit the codebook, write memos, and export your codebook, coding and counts. Your projects are folders on this computer in QualCoder's format, so you can work on them in either program, one at a time. QualCoder is free software for qualitative analysis, of the same kind as NVivo, ATLAS.ti and MAXQDA; Exegete is an independent project, not part of QualCoder and not made by its developers.

Every write is preceded by a backup of the project unless the call asks for none. Exegete runs on this computer and adds no telemetry of its own, but what its tools return enters the conversation and is sent to Anthropic like any other chat content: read PRIVACY.md before you use research data (https://github.com/nicotem/exegete/blob/main/PRIVACY.md). Once a week at most, and when you ask, it fetches a small file from its website, which GitHub hosts, to see whether a newer version exists; nothing from your projects is sent, and the setting "Tell me when a new version is out" switches it off.

The settings choose the tool set (every tool, or a smaller set for local models), the folder where new projects and working copies are kept, your coder name and the AI coder name, whether you also use QualCoder on this computer, and whether Exegete tells you when a new version is out.

toolset.title: Tool set
toolset.description: Type one of two words. full: every tool, creating a new project included (recommended). core: a smaller set for local models. If this shows lifecycle, the earlier name of full, it works as full. Any other word stops the extension from starting.

projects_folder.title: Folder for projects
projects_folder.description: Where new projects are created and working copies of projects are kept. The default, Exegete projects in your home folder (~), is outside Documents, which iCloud or OneDrive may sync; it is made when the first project needs it. If you choose another folder, choose one that no sync service keeps. If this shows QualCoder projects, the earlier default, it keeps working, and Exegete finds the projects there whichever folder you choose. Leaving it empty stops the extension from starting.

coder_name.title: Your coder name
coder_name.description: The name your own codings carry in a project, kept apart from the AI's. Filled in, Exegete gives it to each project it creates, without asking; left empty, Claude asks for it each time. Projects that already exist keep their coder name, or their lack of one. It must differ from the AI coder name. If you also use QualCoder, use the name its settings show as "Current coder", exactly as written there. At most 80 characters; a line break or tab, an invisible formatting character (the joiners some scripts need are allowed) or ##### stops the extension from starting.

ai_coder_name.title: AI coder name
ai_coder_name.description: The name Claude's work in your projects is stored under, so that it stays apart from yours; a model's name lets codings by different models be compared later. Filled in, Exegete gives it to each project it creates, without asking, and offers it first when another project needs one; left empty, Claude asks the first time a project needs it. A project that already has an AI coder name keeps it, and Claude asks you once whether to switch. It must differ from your coder name. At most 80 characters; a line break or tab, an invisible formatting character (the joiners some scripts need are allowed) or ##### stops the extension from starting.

uses_qualcoder.title: Do you also use QualCoder on this computer?
uses_qualcoder.description: Type yes, no or not sure. With yes, Exegete adds some notes that matter only if you also open your projects in QualCoder (such as whether an open QualCoder window shows Exegete's changes, or the backups QualCoder 3.8 may keep elsewhere); with no, it leaves those out, unless a project shows signs that QualCoder may have opened it or QualCoder is running when a project is selected; with not sure, it decides from what it finds on each project and on this computer. Notes worded "if the project is opened in QualCoder", such as the one on emoji and Windows line breaks, are given with any answer, and so is the line saying that a new project is in QualCoder's format. Whatever you answer, Exegete still refuses to write while QualCoder 3.8.2 has a project open, and still warns when it sees signs that QualCoder 4.0 may have one open: an answer can be out of date (a colleague's project, QualCoder installed later), and a write into a project open in QualCoder can lose work. Any other word is read as not sure.

update_check.title: Tell me when a new version is out
update_check.description: Exegete fetches a small file from its website, which GitHub hosts, to see whether a newer version exists: once a week at most on its own, and when Claude checks for you. Claude then tells you once. Nothing from your projects is sent; GitHub records your computer's internet address and the time, as any website does. Switch this off and Exegete itself makes no connection.
